summary: Bitterroot NF hike-in lookout: a c.1930 60-ft pole tower, then a 40-ft L-4 tower by 1940; sites give 1955 destroyed or 1956 torn down. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 60-ft pole tower with 7x7 cab (c.1930), then 40-ft pole tower with L-4 cab (1940)
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1955 per firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; Forest Lookouts says torn down in 1956 with usable parts salvaged

staffing.status: Salmon Mountain District stationed men at Mount Harrington to act as lookouts when not fighting fire; the National Register study gives no year for this

events.note: First tower: 60-ft pole tower with 7x7 cab; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1930, Forest Lookouts gives c.1930
40-ft pole tower with L-4 cab appears in 1940; the sources do not say what happened to the first tower
Listed as destroyed by firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; no cause given
Forest Lookouts says the tower was torn down and usable parts salvaged

evidence.quote: 1930: 60' pole tower with 7x7' cab. 1940: 40' pole L-4 tower. Destroyed 1955.

evidence.supports: first tower 60 ft with cab, dated 1930

corrections.why: 18.3 m (60 ft) is the c.1930 pole tower. Both sites say the lookout stood on a 40-ft (12.2 m) pole tower from 1940 until its end.

resolved_conflicts.field: end of the lookout (1955 destroyed vs 1956 torn down)
resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1955 and destroyed; Forest Lookouts gives 1956, torn down, with usable parts salvaged. The story gives both and records each as its own event. No source gives a cause or explains how the two accounts fit.

sources.title: L-4 Fire Lookouts in the USFS Northern Region (Region 1), 1932-1967 (National Register multiple property documentation form)

notes_for_editor: Dates for the first tower (c.1930) and the 40-ft L-4 tower (1940) agree across the three lookout sites, but the sites appear to share one Kresek-attributed inventory. The end date conflicts: 1955 destroyed (two sites) vs 1956 torn down (Forest Lookouts). The brief's height_m of 18.3 m matches only the 1930 60-ft tower. The National Register passage on Mount Harrington is undated in the text read, so it is recorded as staffing with no event. No source describes the site today and no access rule was found. The brief's access 'unknown' is kept by omitting an access fact. A WebSearch found no newspaper confirmation of the 1955 date.
